CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR
MARCH 1, 2021 AT 3:00 P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE SOLELY BY

In order to facilitate public participation at
meetings held solely by electronic means, the City will accept public comment in
the following manner:
1. Members of the public may submit comments
of any length up to two hours prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Please be aware that, while these comments
will be provided to the members of the body and will become part of the
meeting record, they will not be read aloud. Any comment submitted in this
fashion will be forwarded to the legislative body prior to the start of the
meeting.
2. During the meeting, members of the public
may submit up to 200 words regarding items on the agenda, at the following
webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If you wish your comments to be read aloud
during the meeting, please indicate so on the form. If you submit more than
one form, only the first one received will be read aloud. The City reserves
the right to summarize comments if necessary for the orderly and timely flow
of the meeting. All comments in their entirety will become part of the
meeting record and will be forwarded to the legislative body.

call the City Clerk�s Office at: (626) 744-4124.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 1, 2021 - 3:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo and President Phelps called the Special Joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Unified School
  District (PUSD) Board of Education to order at 3:08 p.m. The
  Pledge of Allegiance was led by PUSD Member Fredericks.
  (Absent: None)

ROLL CALL:
 Council members:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

Pasadena Unified School  President Scott Phelps
District, Board of Education  Vice President Elizabeth Pomeroy
  Member Michelle Richardson Bailey
  Member Kimberly Kenne
  Member Jennifer Hall Lee
  Member Patrick Cahalan
  Member Tina Fredericks

  Staff:  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools
  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Assistant Superintendent of Special
  Education
  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D., Chief Business Officer
  Ana Maria Apodaca, Health Director
  Steven Miller, Ed.D. , Chief Human Resources Officer

  5 MINUTE UPDATE ON COLLABORATE PASADENA

  Steve Mermell , City Manager, provided introductory comments,
  Donald E. Grant Jr. , Executive Director and Geoff Albert,

Council Minutes  03/01/2021
   Community Engagement Specialist, representing Pacific
  Oaks/Collaborate Pasadena,  presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the organization's programs, including Healthy
  Families, Caregiver Engagement, Student Engagement, Early
  Learning and Supportive Communities. They also provided
Councilmember Kennedy  information on their new advocacy efforts related to the
connected to the meeting at  reduction of structural racism and systemic inequities; and
3:21 p.m.  addressing impacts caused by the COVID-19 pandemic; and
  responded to questions.

  In response to Member Kenne's request, Mark Jomsky, City
  Clerk, stated that PowerPoints presented at today's joint
  meeting will be posted online on the City's agenda website.

  Member Kenne spoke on the need for the PUSD Board
  Members, City Council, and community partners to come
  together on a regular basis to discuss issues in the community.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  5 MINUTE UPDATE ON YOUTH MASTER PLAN

  President Phelps provided introductory comments, and Christy
  Zamani, Executive Director of Day One, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation and video (with various PUSD/Pasadena City
  College students) on the Youth Master Plan, summarizing the
  group's progress on various priority areas and next steps; and
  responded to questions.

  In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry related to how the City
  Council can move the Youth Master Plan forward and provide
  support for this work, Ms. Zamani responded that a
  representative from both the PUSD and City attending
  partnership meetings and collaborating with Day One to support
  youth in Pasadena would be a great help.

  President Phelps and Mayor Gordo asked PUSD and City staff
  to coordinate with Ms. Zamani and ensure that staff from both
  agencies attend the next partnership meeting.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that a letter providing
  comments/suggestions on the matter, including the need to
  address the needs of the children in PUSD Schools, from Lisa
  J. Cavalier, representing Boys & Girls Club of Pasadena, was
  received and distributed to the City Council and School Board,
  posted on-line, and made part of the public record.

Council Minutes  2  03/01 /2021
   He also read aloud comments and suggestions on the matter
  from the following individuals:

  Allen 8. Shay, Pasadena resident
  Nancy, Pasadena resident
  Daniel Fong, Pasadena resident
  Claudia Hathcock, Pasadena resident

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the importance of staff to be mindful
  of transitioning back to in-class instruction for the students,
  which he believes will lead to some behavioral changes.

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's request related to
  information on the City's Summer Rose Program funds, City
  Manager Mermell responded that he will confirm the fund
  balance with staff and distribute the information in the weekly
  letter; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy stated that he would like to see
  additional diversity in the outward looking faces of the videos.
  He spoke on the need for the City Council to determine, in light
  of the COVI D-19 pandemic, how to provide resources, stipends,
  etc., to support those young individuals who are
  disproportionally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, such as
  those that can perform jobs needed by non-profit organizations
  or the City of Pasadena to provide students with nominal
  resources.

  President Phelps requested that Elizabeth Blanco, Assistant
  Superintendent of Special Education, determine why the
  students are having difficulty signing up for life-skill/Home
  Economics and Financial Literacy courses, and provide
  assistance to the students that would like to schedule such
  courses.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed .

  5 MINUTE UPDATE ON THE OFFICE OF THE YOUNG CHILD

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and
  Carla Hegwood, Office of the Young Child Coordinator,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the City's Master Plan
  for the Young Child; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the importance of the
  position of the Office of the Young Child Coordinator, and asked
  Ms. Hegwood to commit to three years of service in the position
  to establish a work plan and ensure continuity for the position.

Council Minutes  3  03/01/2021
   Councilmember Rivas suggested that the Office of the Young
  Child work with local healthcare providers to connect with
  families with young children throughout the community.

  Member Frederick spoke on her hope that PUSD provides free
  daycare and preschool to the community, and believes a strong
  partnership with the Office of the Young Child is a good starting
  point to achieve such a goal.

  Michelle Perera, Director of Libraries and Information Services,
  provided information on the City libraries that were selected to
  participate in creating and cultivating a race equity and inclusion
  initiative, with staff to analyze the City's library programs to
  determine how the City can better serve the community through
  an equity viewpoint; and responded to questions.

  President Phelps suggested a collaboration effort with PUS □
  and City staff to analyze the future of preschools in PUSD.

  Elizabeth Blanco, Assistant Superintend of Special Education,
  provided information on PUSD's partnerships with many of the
  City coordinators and programs; and stated she looks forward to
  working with Ms. Hegwood.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the need to constantly reinvent the
  City's libraries, and redefine important roles in the community to
  involve critical infrastructures.

  Mayor Gordo requested an update on the Early Development
  Instrument (EDI) and Early Childhood Hubs (i.e. the number of
  participants, outreach, etc.) data reports. He spoke on the need
  for staff to address the City's policies on COVID-19 and social
  equity impacts to young children in the community, which he
  believes is a developmental issue. He reported to the City
  Council and public his plans to appoint an advisory body to
  provide a better understanding of the various COVID-19 and
  social equity impact issues, including mental health, and
  requested that staff and PUS □ Board Members suggest
  appointees to serve on the advisory body.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  PRESENTATION ON THE PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT MAGNET

  President Phelps provided introductory comments, and Helen
  Hill, Director of Curriculum, Instruction and Professional
  Development, and Shannon Mumolo, Signature Programs

Council Minutes  4  03/01/2021
   Coordinator, both representing PUSD, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the item; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Masuda requested data on the number of high
  school students that are participating in college courses and the
  length of the courses.

  Member Hall Lee reported that Dr. Ying Ying Goh is the keynote
  speaker at the Women's History Month Assembly, hosted by Lori
  Touloumian, Principal of Eliot Arts Magnet Academy, and PUSD
  Board Member Hall Lee, to be held virtually on March 24, 2021 .

  Member Pomeroy stated that all schools in Altadena and Sierra
  Madre, including Magnet Schools, are open and available to all
  Pasadena residents.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the need to determine what action can
  be taken to encourage the extension of the Magnet Programs
  throughout the City's public school system. He asked
  Councilmember Madison to agendize for discussion, at a future
  Legislative Policy Committee meeting, an action that the City
  Council can take to support legislation related to schools
  applying for additional Magnet Program funding. Mayor Gordo
  spoke on the need to better coordinate legislative efforts
  between the City, PUSD, and Pasadena City College.

  President Phelps spoke on the need for additional internship
  opportunities in the City, which is a possible career establishing
  prospect for students attending PUSD schools.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  PRESENTATION ON THE REOPENING OF SCHOOLS IN
  THE PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT

  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools provided
  introductory comments and thanked Dr. Goh, City staff, and
  community partners for all their efforts to serve and support
  PUSD; and Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Assistant Superintendent
  of Special Education, and Ana Maria Apodaca, Health Director,
  and Leslie Barnes, Ed.D., Chief Business Officer, all with PUSD,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions.

  Dr. McDonald reported that in light of the announcement by
  Governor Newsom announcing plans to reopen grades K-6 in
  mid-March, PUSD Board of Education will schedule a special
  meeting on Thursday, March 4, 2021, so that he may offer a

Council Minutes  5  03/01/2021
   recommendation for PUSD students to return to in-person
  learning; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Hampton recommended that PUSD staff
  contact the Rose Bowl Operating Company and Pasadena City
  College to determine if PUSD high school senior athletes can
  use available sports fields in the area to enable them to play
  sports, display and record their athletic capabilities, and allow
  them to apply/earn college scholarship offers. He asked staff to
  work collaboratively with PUSD to determine if the Rose Bowl
  Stadium or the Jackie Robinson fields may be offered to PUSD
  high school sport teams. He encouraged PUSD to offer summer
  school for students who would like to earn extra school credit. In
  addition, he asked PUSD staff to share information on lessons
  learned during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  City Manager Mermell stated that the City is in communication
  with Darryl Dunn, Chief Executive Officer at the Rose Bowl
  Stadium, and that the City is eager to assist wherever possible
  to locate available sports playing fields for PUSD students.

  Steven Miller, Ed.D., Chief Human Resources Officer, provided
  information on the number of substitute teachers working for
  PUSD.

  Dr. Ying Ying Goh, Director of Public Health, provided
  information on Los Angeles County's guidance on school grades
  that will be permitted to participate in in-person learning (based
  on the percentage of case rates, trajectory of new positive
  cases, etc.); information on school requirements to open for in-
  person learning; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Williams requested information on the number
  of private schools in Pasadena.
President Phelps was excused
and disconnected from the  Member Cahalan encouraged the community to continue
meeting at 5:52 p.m.  abiding by the COVID-19 safety guidelines and to get
  vaccinated.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the importance of completing upgrades
  to PUSD sport fields to enable high school athletics
  activities/games; and expressed concerns with "club" groups
  and sports activities from outside of Pasadena using PUSD
  fields. He asked PUSD staff to provide information on the
  number of hours that have been dedicated to non-Pasadena
  club teams and the impacts these activities have had on the
  fields, including cost recovery information; and stated that he
  does not believe PUSD should allow organizations outside of
  Pasadena to use PUSD sports fields.

Council Minutes  6  03/01/2021
   City Clerk Jomsky reported that a number of letters and emails
  expressing concerns with opening of schools; advocating for an
  immediate reopening of schools or a phase-in approach to the
  reopening of schools in Pasadena; and/or advocating for the
  reopening of public pools in the City; were received, distributed
  to the City Council and Board of Education, posted on-line, and
  made part of the public record from the following individuals:

  PUSD employee and Pasadena resident
  Katina Mandavia, residence not stated
  Linda Chan, residence not stated
  Mary Shimazaki, residence not stated
  David Berk, Teacher at Hamilton Elementary School
  Cassandra Williams, residence not stated
  Tarah Kenedy, PUSD parent
  Erika Foy, on behalf of Save California Students Now
  Barrett Snider, residence not stated
  Mary Forrest, Pasadena resident

  In addition, the City Clerk, read aloud comments expressing
  concerns with opening of schools; advocating for an immediate
  opening of schools or a phase-in approach to the reopening of
  schools in Pasadena; advocating for PUSD teacher pay raises,
  and providing comments/suggestions from the following
  individuals:

  Cynthia Lake, Pasadena resident
  Denise R. Johnson, Altadena resident
  Mary, Pasadena resident
  Edward Magalong, Pasadena resident
  Linda Chan, Pasadena resident
  Tarah Kennedy, Pasadena resident
  Neil and Shaina Tyler, Altadena resident
  Kathleen Bergman, Covina resident
  Beth A. Strehl, Pasadena resident
  Kai Venable, Pasadena resident
  David Berk, Pasadena resident
  Hayley Boaz, residence not stated
  Erika Foy, Pasadena resident
  Ryan Forrest, Pasadena resident
  Mary Forrest, Pasadena resident
  Angela Buchanan, Pasadena resident
  Sylvia Salas, Pasadena resident
  Jennifer Vane, Pasadena resident
  David Chavez, Pasadena resident
  John Michelena, Pasadena resident
  Diana Morrison, Pasadena resident
  Diana Arnold, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  7  03/01/2021
   Member Bailey voiced safety concerns for teachers who do not
  yet feel comfortable in returning to in-person learning; and
  expressed concerns with the PUSD Board and the City Council
  in taking sides on the reopening of schools at this moment; and
  stated her preference that the Board and City Council
  concentrate on school safety and ensuring that teachers are
  safe and can be vaccinated.

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke on the need to develop an
  informational/educational campaign to provide updated data to
  the community, students, parents and teachers on the facts
  related to COVID-19.

  Councilmember Kennedy recommended children of a certain
  age group return to in-class learning, and advocated that
  teaching staff receive access to be vaccinated, so everyone is
  comfortable returning to in-person learning.

  Member Fredericks advocated for teachers and their family
  members to be vaccinated in order to ease the fears of teachers
  and staff of the possibility of spreading COVI D-19 to their family
  members; and echoed comments made by Member Bailey
  related to COVID-19 transmission fears from PUSD teachers
  and staff. She also spoke on the need to include PUSD teachers
  and staff in the discussions regarding the reopening of schools,
  including conducting walkthroughs focused on COVID-19 safety
  protocols and preparations for the classrooms.

  Mayor Gordo stated that he believes that part of the fear factor
  of COVI D-19 is the lack of information from school districts; and
  spoke on the need for the planning on the reopening of schools
  to be distributed to the community. He encouraged PUSD staff
  to put a plan together on the reopening of schools for students
  in grades K through 12 with an opportunity for the public to
  provide input. Mayor Gordo also encouraged PUSD staff to
  provide a written recommendation related to the reopening of
  schools to the PUSD Board Members, prior to the Thursday,
  March 4, 2021 meeting so that the community may be informed
  in advance of the meeting. He asked staff to work with
  independent schools to ensure they provide return to school
  safety plans for grades K through 12.

  The City Council and PUSD Board members discussed issues
  related to the safe reopening of schools; how best to ensure the
  safety of students and teachers; what preconditions should be
  established prior to the reopening of PUSD schools; mental
  health support services that should be in place for children
  affected by COVID-19; and issues related to the fears and
  concerns of reopening schools too soon.

Council Minutes  8  03/01/2021
   Councilmember Williams encouraged the PUSD Board to open
  the schools as soon as they can safely be opened.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  Member Bailey announced that on Saturday, March 20, 2021 a
  virtual STEAM symposium will be held online, and encouraged
  those needing additional information to please contact PUSD;
  and reported that the NAACP - Pasadena Chapter, working
  along with Huntington Hospital, will be providing vaccinations to
  eligible members of the public and teachers who are interested.

ADJOURNMENT  On the order of the President and Mayor, the special joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Board of Education
  adjourned at 8:28 p.m. in memory of all those that are ill and
  have lost their lives during the COVID-19 pandemic

  Victor M. Gordo, Mayo
  City of Pasadena
